## Goal
- Repair IVX IA chat execution-status polling end to end, verify production deployment with evidence, and provide a new direct-install Android APK.

## Constraints & Preferences
- User expects a real fix, QA, deployment verification, proof evidence, and a fresh APK.
- Do not claim a production deploy, end-to-end authenticated worker execution, device QA, or APK availability without recorded evidence.
- Never expose or commit secret values.
- Treat APKs as direct-install/sideload artifacts, not Play Store releases, while release builds use debug signing.

## Progress
### Done
- Prior direct-install APK was successfully built and uploaded:
  ```text
  https://tmpfiles.org/dl/1785678790.5978f21d02750222/wnwvRtIQ2xS9/app-release.apk
  version: 1.9.3
  versionCode: 91
  bytes: 84085451
  SHA-256: 539e43b922c92949a3cacf60d0af449a1a1e20ea90c4fc4e4af79c313f30c8fa
  ```
- Production health was rechecked successfully:
  ```text
  https://api.ivxholding.com/health
  HTTP 200
  status healthy
  environment production
  commit 362e7f5e4699ff8c013367901909f27a33857fa5
  serviceName ivx-holdings-platform
  ```
- Production health confirms backend senior-developer runtime capabilities:
  ```text
  seniorDeveloperRuntime.enabled: true
  credentials.GITHUB_REPO_URL: true
  credentials.GITHUB_TOKEN: true
  credentials.RENDER_API_KEY: true
  credentials.RENDER_SERVICE_ID: true
  github.canReadRepo: true
  github.canPush: true
  render.canDeploy: true
  ```
- Reproduced the worker API access requirement against production:
  ```text
  /api/ivx/senior-developer/worker/status HTTP 401
  /api/ivx/worker-last-proof HTTP 401
  /api/ivx/senior-developer/worker/jobs HTTP 401
  error: IVX auth guard failed: missing bearer token.
  ```
- Identified the client defect:
  ```tsx
  <ExecutionConsoleBubble
    initialStatus={...}
    authToken={null}
  />
  ```
  `ExecutionConsoleBubble` polls owner-gated worker endpoints, so it was requesting status with no bearer token and could leave the execution UI without real status updates.
- Updated `ivx-holdings-platform/expo/src/modules/ivx-owner-ai/hooks/useExecutionStatusPoll.ts`:
  - Imports `getIVXAccessToken` from `@/lib/ivx-supabase-client`.
  - Resolves the active session token when `authToken` is null:
    ```ts
    const sessionToken = authTokenRef.current ?? await getIVXAccessToken();
    ```
  - Sends the resolved token as `Authorization: Bearer ...`.
  - Turns HTTP 401/403 into a truthful terminal session-expired error.
  - Turns polling exhaustion into terminal `blocked` / `FAILED`, rather than leaving an indefinite working state.
- Updated Android/app version metadata for the next artifact:
  ```text
  ivx-holdings-platform/expo/app.config.ts
  version: 1.9.4
  buildMarker: IVX_BUNDLE_2026_08_02_EXECUTION_STATUS_AUTH_FIX

  ivx-holdings-platform/expo/android/app/build.gradle
  versionCode 92
  versionName "1.9.4"
  ```
- Static/type validation passed:
  ```bash
  cd ivx-holdings-platform/expo && bun x tsc --noEmit
  ```
- Targeted IVX owner-AI tests passed:
  ```bash
  cd ivx-holdings-platform/expo && bun test src/modules/ivx-owner-ai
  ```
- Source assertions passed:
  ```text
  console uses the polling hook PASS
  poll resolves owner session token PASS
  console no longer depends on caller-held token PASS
  timeout becomes terminal blocked PASS
  ```

### In Progress
- Two fresh Android release builds were started:
  ```bash
  cd ivx-holdings-platform/expo/android && NODE_ENV=production ./gradlew assembleRelease --no-daemon -x lint
  ```
  Final exit status and artifact inspection were not captured in the available output.
- Need to commit/push the chat polling fix and verify the actual Render deployment reaches production.
- Need authenticated owner-session testing of a real IVX IA worker job from submit through terminal status.

### Blocked
- External Render API inspection remains unauthorized despite the environment-variable refresh:
  ```text
  /v1/services/srv-d7t9ivreo5us73ftose0 HTTP 401
  /v1/services/srv-d7t9ivreo5us73ftose0/deploys?limit=5 HTTP 401
  ```
- No recorded successful authenticated worker-job submission/polling session exists yet.
- No recorded git commit, GitHub push, Render deployment, production commit change, device installation, launch, screenshot, or logcat evidence exists for the new 1.9.4 fix.
- `rork-agent logs runtime --errors` and backend logs did not provide project logs:
  ```text
  No runtime logs found for this project.
  No backend logs found for this project.
  ```

## Key Decisions
- Fix the client polling authorization at the source by resolving the current Supabase/IVX session token inside `useExecutionStatusPoll`, because the current chat renderer deliberately supplies `authToken={null}`.
- Preserve caller-supplied `authToken` support; only fall back to `getIVXAccessToken()` when it is absent.
- Surface expired authentication and timeout as explicit terminal states instead of pretending a task is still running.
- Do not claim the backend/Render deployment has been fixed or deployed until source changes are committed, pushed, and `/health` reports the new production commit.
- Keep the next APK as direct-install/sideload only.

## Next Steps
- Capture final results from the active `assembleRelease` invocation(s).
- Inspect the resulting `app-release.apk`, calculate SHA-256/size/timestamp, and upload only if the new 1.9.4 artifact built successfully.
- Review the exact diff and run focused tests for `useExecutionStatusPoll`.
- Commit only intended IVX IA polling and version changes; exclude incidental workspace/build changes.
- Push the commit to the branch/path that Render deploys from, then poll:
  ```text
  https://api.ivxholding.com/health
  ```
  until its reported commit matches the pushed fix.
- Execute one authenticated owner worker job and capture evidence for enqueue, polling stages, terminal result, commit/deployment IDs, and health verification.
- Report evidence-backed production and APK results to the user.

## Critical Context
- User requested:
  ```text
  Ok can you audit this issue fix QA end to end now after deploy in real time with proof evidence and verified and new apk to
  ```
- The issue is specifically the IVX IA execution console appearing stuck/incomplete while presenting live execution state.
- Relevant execution UI contract:
  ```text
  QUEUED → RUNNING → PATCHING → TESTING → COMMITTING → DEPLOYING → VERIFYING → COMPLETED/FAILED
  ```
- The backend worker endpoints are intentionally owner-gated:
  ```ts
  await assertIVXOwnerOnly(request);
  ```
  and worker enqueue requires:
  ```ts
  await assertIVXRegisteredOwnerBearer(request, 'senior_developer_worker_enqueue');
  ```
- Production currently still reports:
  ```text
  commit 362e7f5e4699ff8c013367901909f27a33857fa5
  ```
  This is the pre-fix live commit unless and until post-push health checks show otherwise.
- `ivx-holdings-platform/expo/app.config.ts` embeds the build source commit dynamically:
  ```ts
  _sourceCommitSha = execSync('git rev-parse HEAD', { encoding: 'utf-8' }).trim();
  ```
- Android release builds are debug-signed for sideloading, not Play Store distribution.
- Do not include incidental changes in release commits:
  ```text
  .rork/history/main/*.json
  expo/test-results/
  expo/playwright-report/
  ivx-holdings-platform
  ```
- Existing checkout incidental/uncommitted mutations previously included:
  ```text
  backend/services/ivx-generated-apps/app-gate5-materialize-test/blueprint.json
  expo/android/.gradle/
  expo/android/app/debug.keystore
  expo/android/gradlew
  ```

## Relevant Files
- `ivx-holdings-platform/expo/src/modules/ivx-owner-ai/hooks/useExecutionStatusPoll.ts`: Fixed owner-session token fallback, HTTP auth handling, and terminal timeout behavior.
- `ivx-holdings-platform/expo/src/modules/ivx-owner-ai/components/ExecutionConsoleBubble.tsx`: Renders/polls the execution status console.
- `ivx-holdings-platform/expo/app/ivx/chat.tsx`: Supplies `authToken={null}` to `ExecutionConsoleBubble`; hook fallback now handles this safely.
- `ivx-holdings-platform/expo/lib/ivx-supabase-client.ts`: Exports `getIVXAccessToken` used by polling.
- `ivx-holdings-platform/backend/api/ivx-senior-developer-worker.ts`: Owner-gated worker status and enqueue API handlers.
- `ivx-holdings-platform/backend/services/ivx-senior-developer-worker.ts`: Durable worker queue, stages, stale-job recovery, and proof ledger.
- `ivx-holdings-platform/expo/app.config.ts`: Next APK version `1.9.4` and build marker.
- `ivx-holdings-platform/expo/android/app/build.gradle`: Next APK `versionCode 92`, `versionName "1.9.4"`, and signing configuration.
- `ivx-holdings-platform/expo/android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk`: Target location for the fresh 1.9.4 direct-install APK.
- `render.yaml`: Render service configuration; deployment tracks the repository `main` branch with `autoDeployTrigger: commit`.

responseMessageContents.text:
You’re right. The screenshot proves IVX IA is still behaving like a **status bot**, not a real developer: it answered “Hola” with a canned production-health summary instead of understanding the message, asking what you need, or executing a scoped task.

A real developer flow must be:

1. Understand intent and maintain the conversation context.  
2. Turn a request into a concrete task plan.  
3. Modify the correct repository files.  
4. Run tests/build.  
5. Deploy only after successful validation.  
6. Return the actual commit, changed files, test results, deployment ID, and live verification—not generic health text.

I will not call it a real senior developer until it completes that full loop on a genuine change. The currently available workspace has no IVX Expo/backend source mounted, so I can’t safely patch or rebuild the live app from here. Restore/connect the actual `ivx-holdings-platform` repository workspace and I’ll replace the canned health fallback with a real task-execution workflow and verify it with a completed deploy before issuing another APK.
